test_title: PYST 32: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 25 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: Two pipes X and Y can fill a tank in 14 hours and 21 hours, respectively. Both pipes are opened simultaneously to fill the tank. In how many hours will the empty tank be filled?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM of 14 and 21 = 42 units.

Combined efficiency of X and Y = (42 ÷ 14) + (42 ÷ 21) = 3 + 2 = 5 units/hour.

Time required to fill the tank = Total Work ÷ Combined efficiency = 42 ÷ 5 = 8 (2/5) hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 (2/5) hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by pipe X = 14 hours

Time taken by pipe Y = 21 hours

**Method Used:**

Total Work is considered as the LCM of the individual times taken by the pipes to fill the tank independently.

 **Hours**

 X

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Efficiency of X and Y together = 3 + 2 = 5 units/hour

⇒ Total Time taken = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Total Time taken = 42 ÷ 5

⇒ Total Time taken = 8 (2/5) hours

**∴ The correct answer is 8 (2/5) hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Concept

It operates on the same logic as Time and Work. If a pipe fills a tank in x hours, its 1 hour work is 1/x part of the total capacity.

Emptying Pipe / Leakage

If a pipe or leak empties a tank in y hours, its 1 hour work is considered negative (−1/y). Net filling work = (1/x − 1/y).

Alternating Pipes

When two pipes are opened alternately for one hour each, compute the total work done in a 2-hour cycle and scale it up near the total capacity before calculating the final step.
